description: The events a security officer wants to see first: failed sign-ins and brute force attempts, staff signing in on behalf of users and tenants, API keys, admin rights, new users, invites, transfers, deactivations and password resets, deletions and exports, webhook subscriptions (an outbound channel for the data) and refused file downloads, cross-account attempts among them. Everything here is category audit.

panels.description: user.login_failed. The e-mail of the attempt is stored hashed only.
panels.title: Failed sign-ins

panels.description: user.login_as and tenant.login_as: somebody acted under another identity.
panels.title: Staff sign-ins as users

panels.description: api_key.create: a new credential that lives until revoked.
panels.title: API keys created

panels.description: api_key.revoke.
panels.title: API keys revoked

panels.description: user.admin_toggle.
panels.title: Admin rights changed

panels.description: user.deactivate.
panels.title: Users deactivated

panels.description: file.access_denied: the permission check of the backend said no.
panels.title: Refused downloads

panels.description: template.export: process definitions left the system as a file.
panels.title: Template exports

panels.description: group.delete, template.delete and workflow.terminate.
panels.title: Deletions

panels.description: webhook.subscribe and webhook.unsubscribe: a subscription sends the events of an account to an outside URL.
panels.title: Webhook subscriptions changed

panels.description: Refused downloads where the file belongs to another account than the one asking.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="pneumatic-file-service", deployment_environment=~"$environment", account_id=~"$account_id"} | event_type="file.access_denied" | label_format cross="{{ if ne .payload_file_account_id .account_id }}yes{{ else }}no{{ end }}" | cross="yes" [$__range]))

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (pii_ip, payload_reason) (count_over_time({service_name=~"pneumatic-.*", deployment_environment=~"$environment", account_id=~"$account_id"} | event_type="user.login_failed" [$__range])))

panels.description: Ten e-mails with the most failed attempts. The e-mail itself is never stored, only its SHA-256; the first twelve characters tell the targets apart.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (h) (count_over_time({service_name=~"pneumatic-.*", deployment_environment=~"$environment", account_id=~"$account_id"} | event_type="user.login_failed" | label_format h="{{ substr 0 12 .payload_email_hash }}" [$__range])))
